content:
sara_oncall: noticed increased 5xx from eu-north1 serving tier ~10:45 UTC. telemetry shows spike in packet loss to the peering fabric and several GPU pools reporting control-plane disconnects. marking as P1 and tagging network/infra.

arjun_infra: seeing the same. BGP sessions to ISP-ALPHA are flapping. multiple routes to the eu-north1 edge are being withdrawn intermittently. some pods are stuck in Terminating due to lost k8s api connectivity.

maya_network: traceroutes show AS path oscillation between AS64512 <-> AS65021. looks like upstream is re-advertising a /24 intermittently. attaching quick output: ```traceroute to 3.12.45.67 (3.12.45.67), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets\n 1  10.0.0.1  0.4 ms 0.3 ms 0.3 ms\n 2  198.51.100.1  4.5 ms 4.6 ms 4.4 ms\n 3  * * *\n 4  203.0.113.5  12.3 ms 12.4 ms 12.6 ms\n```

arjun_infra: running healthcheck scripts across GPU nodepool: `./scripts/check-gpu-pools --region eu-north1`. Several nodes report kubelet disconnect and nv_peer_mem errors. I'm starting a controlled drain of the most-affected nodes to avoid noisy evictions.

sara_oncall: @lia_support can you draft a short status page and notify Tier 1 customers? keep it factual: "investigating peering instability affecting eu-north1; mitigations in progress". no SLA calc yet until we confirm failover capacity.

lia_support: draft status update below. please thumbs if ok: 
"We are investigating network instability affecting our eu-north1 region causing increased errors and higher latency for some customers. Our engineering teams are actively mitigating by shifting traffic and draining impacted nodes. We will post updates every 15 minutes. No action required from customers at this time." :warning:

arjun_infra: initiating traffic steering: enabling route-policy fallback to prefer eu-west1 replicas for affected customers and enabling model-variant fallback (quantized model v1q) for latency-sensitive paths. Doing a canary shift (5% -> 20%) then full until healthy.

maya_network: coordinated with ISP-ALPHA NOC; they confirm a flapping session tied to a maintenance churn in their peering fabric. they advised to shift traffic off the peering link while they stabilize — ETA from them ~30-45m.

sara_oncall: ok proceed with full shift plan. enable temporary rate-limits on job-queue accepts for new reserved jobs in eu-north1 to reduce pressure. post the status update now.

lia_support: posted status page: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incident/eu-north1-peering. also opened high-priority support tickets for customers with active Dedicated capacity and emailed top 10 accounts with account managers on CC.

arjun_infra: hands-on checklist: 1) drain affected nodes (in progress) 2) steer traffic via router-control to eu-west1 3) enable fallback model variants 4) monitor token consumption/cost delta 5) prepare rollback if route shuffle causes regressions. running `routerctl shift --from eu-north1 --to eu-west1 --percent 20` now.

deploy-bot: automatic action: recent network config change (AS-path filter change) detected at 1887659400 — rolled back on detection. No new deploys allowed to network tier until incident clears.

sara_oncall: next update in 15m or sooner if ISP confirms. current customer impact: increased errors (5xx) for ~12% of requests in eu-north1, elevated latency for another ~18%. ETA from ISP ~30-45m but internal shift should restore service for most customers within ~20-30m. logging all actions to the incident doc. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
